clue.text: Winning deputy, good and respectable

parts.note: a side that is winning is up, ahead in the game
a deputy is a stand-in for someone else

explanation.surface: A praise of some successful second-in-command who is decent and well regarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an honest, decent, law-abiding person is described as respectable.

clue.text: Code name — 'Omaha' — Turing covers up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the concealed letters are read from bottom to top
the two quoted words cover, that is conceal, the letters strung across their join

explanation.surface: A wartime cryptography scene: Alan Turing hushing up a codename.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' conceals HATU across 'Omaha' and 'Turing'; 'up' turns it round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the D-Day landing beaches had code names, and this was one of them, alongside Omaha.

clue.text: Prune others growing wild, indefinite number

indicators.note: plants growing wild sprawl out of order, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: cut back the other plants that are running riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to prune something is to cut it back or make it shorter.

clue.text: Desperate to know how to proceed and make amends, put cards in post

definitions.text: Desperate to know how to proceed

parts.note: to make amends for a wrong is to atone

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a card is a witty, amusing person, so cards are wits

explanation.surface: Someone at a loss who decides to apologise by mailing greetings cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cards' here are jokers, not greetings cards: WITS goes 'in' SEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being at a loss and unable to work out what to do next is exactly this state.

clue.text: Plain individual

definitions.meaning: plain in the sense of clear and easy to see
individual as in separate and different from the rest

explanation.surface: Description of a person who is ordinary and on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of the word: clearly perceptible, and separate or discrete from others.

clue.text: Antelope present in many a land

indicators.note: the answer is present within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A wildlife fact: this antelope is found across many countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an African antelope with spiral horns, a member of the antelope family.

clue.text: Struggle with scene

parts.note: to struggle against a rival is to vie

explanation.surface: Wrestling with a scene, like an artist battling a difficult landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a scene laid out before you is a prospect or vista.

clue.text: Elected head of trustees, impolite to butt in

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in office

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: impolite means rude

explanation.surface: A newly chosen chair of a board who is rude enough to interrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to butt in is to interrupt or force yourself into a situation uninvited.

clue.text: Almost get the better of more fashionable one seen in church

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is left off

parts.note: to worst someone is to defeat them
hipper means more trendy

explanation.surface: Someone nearly outdoing a trendier person at a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a churchgoer attending a service is someone who prays and venerates.

clue.text: In love, you and me after a second run out

indicators.note: after places the pair for you and me at the end

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A romantic couple whose time together is running out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter dismissed 'run out' is recorded as RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being in love, someone is affectionate and passionate.

clue.text: Judge arrives carrying grip

indicators.note: one word carries the other inside it

parts.note: ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrives
a bite is a firm grip, as of a tyre on the road

explanation.surface: A judge turns up at court carrying a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a referee or umpire who settles disputes is a judge.

clue.text: Various small things of interest to a coin collector?

definitions.meaning: odds and ends, assorted small items

definitions.text: of interest to a coin collector?
definitions.meaning: old coins were called bits (threepenny bit) and pieces (pieces of eight)

explanation.surface: Odds and ends that a numismatist would like to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for odds and ends, and literally coins, as in threepenny bits and pieces of eight.

clue.text: Hi-tech duo's ATM fiddling shows a gift for making money

indicators.note: fiddling with something tampers with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two tech wizards rigging a cash machine prove they can make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddling' rearranges all thirteen letters of HITECHDUOSATM.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: King Midas turned all he touched to gold, so the phrase means a knack for profit.

clue.text: Form of treatment that may be shown in photo, as yet to be developed

indicators.note: a photo to be developed in the darkroom is changed, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A treatment that might show up in a photograph not yet processed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: manipulating bones and joints is a recognised kind of complementary therapy.

clue.text: Pack in place in Kent

definitions.meaning: to squeeze something tightly between two others
a historic town in Kent, one of the Cinque Ports

explanation.surface: Crowding visitors into a town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to wedge between two things, and a town in Kent, the English county in the south-east.

clue.text: Create and settle differences

definitions.meaning: to invent, as one invents a story
to be reconciled after a quarrel

explanation.surface: Instructions to build something and then patch up a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Two phrasal-verb senses: to invent or fabricate, and to be reconciled after a quarrel.

clue.text: Pour alcoholic drink, drowning insect

indicators.note: the drink drowns the insect by holding it inside

parts.note: beer is an alcoholic drink
a moth is an insect

explanation.surface: Pouring a pint only to find a fly drowning in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The British phrase means to pour the tea for everyone, as the host does.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: taking charge of serving tea from the pot is to pour it out for everyone.

clue.text: Grounds of Parisian art gallery

parts.note: French es means of, as in docteur es lettres
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: The gardens belonging to a gallery in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the land and grounds belonging to a country house make up its property.

clue.text: Blunder among reserves in ground

indicators.note: one piece goes among, so inside, the other

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's army reserve
to blunder is to err
taken as it stands

explanation.surface: A military mistake by reservists out on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was the British volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stretch of land and its physical features is the lie of the land.

clue.text: Endless sex entertaining a jolly foreign policeman

indicators.note: one piece entertains, so holds, the other
endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: sex as in male or female is gender
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A racy tale of an officer abroad and a cheerful escapade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims GENDER to GENDE; 'entertaining' puts ARM inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a French police officer is the classic foreign policeman.

clue.text: Unnerve leader of ramble, pointing to snake

parts.note: to unnerve someone is to rattle them

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A walk leader alarmed after spotting a snake on the path.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal name: a rattlesnake is commonly called by this shortened name.

clue.text: Pedant tense? No, it's I, corrected

parts.note: the perfect is a grammatical tense

indicators.note: corrected means put right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fussy grammarian protesting that it should be 'it is I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Close synonym: a stickler who insists on everything being exactly right is a pedant.

clue.text: Hard to penetrate word for unit of heat

indicators.note: one piece penetrates, so goes inside, the other

parts.note: a term is a word
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tricky scientific word that is difficult to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an old British unit of heat, used for gas billing, equal to 100,000 BTU.

clue.text: Close to body dropping temperature

indicators.note: dropping means taking out a letter

parts.note: the torso is the trunk of the body

explanation.surface: A fever breaking: someone near death as their temperature falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a phrase meaning approximately or roughly, as in ten minutes give or take.

clue.text: Time to walk like a duck? Nonsense

parts.note: ducks waddle

explanation.surface: A silly question about when to start walking like a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: silly or pretentious talk is rubbish or drivel.

clue.text: One could upset speaker — he upset clerk

parts.note: taken as it stands

indicators.note: an upset is turned over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outburst at a meeting: the speaker unsettled, then a clerk upset too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' appears twice: the first belongs to the definition, the second rearranges CLERK into CKLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: someone who interrupts and barracks a public speaker can rattle them.

clue.text: Pull domesticated ox round rear of barn

indicators.note: the ox goes round the letter

parts.note: the yak is a Himalayan ox domesticated for milk and haulage

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A farmer hauling a tame ox round the back of the barn.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to yank is to pull sharply.

clue.text: Opera company's manager breaking a promise to tour Rhode Island

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go on tour round the state abbreviation
breaking scatters the letters of the words that follow

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: An opera manager failing to keep a promise to take the company to Rhode Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' scrambles the eight letters to IMPRESAO, and the state's two letters slip in before the final O.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an impresario organises and finances operas, concerts and shows.
